# demo-todo

A tiny Node todo list with due dates, priorities, tags, search, recurring items and JSON persistence. It ships as an ES module library (`src/todo.js`) and a CLI (`bin/todo.js`). No dependencies.

Run the tests with `npm test`.

## Library API

```js
import { TodoList, PRIORITIES, RECURRENCES, nextDue } from "./src/todo.js";
```

### Item shape

```js
{
  id: 1,
  title: "Write docs",
  done: false,
  due: "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z", // ISO string or null
  priority: "normal",              // "low" | "normal" | "high"
  tags: ["work"],                  // present once a tag has been added
  repeat: "weekly",                // present only on recurring items
  repeatDay: 1                     // anchor day-of-month (UTC) for recurring items
}
```

### Exports

| Export | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `PRIORITIES` | `["low", "normal", "high"]` |
| `RECURRENCES` | `["daily", "weekly", "monthly"]` |
| `TodoList` | The list class (below) |
| `nextDue(due, repeat, day)` | Compute the next due date for a recurrence |

### `new TodoList()`

Creates an empty list with `items = []` and `nextId = 1`.

### `list.add(title, { due, priority = "normal" } = {})` -> item

Adds an item and returns it. `due` may be a `Date` or anything `new Date()` accepts; it is stored as an ISO string (or `null` if omitted). Throws if `title` is empty, `priority` is not in `PRIORITIES`, or `due` is invalid.

```js
const list = new TodoList();
list.add("Buy milk");
list.add("File taxes", { due: "2026-04-15", priority: "high" });
```

### `list.complete(id)` -> item

Marks the item done and returns it. Throws if the id is not found.

### `list.pending()` -> item[]

Returns items that are not done.

### `list.clear()`

Removes all completed items.

### `list.sorted(now = new Date())` -> item[]

Returns a sorted copy of the items: overdue (not done, due before `now`) first, then priority high to low, then due date ascending (no due date last), then id.

### Tags

Tags are trimmed and lowercased.

- `list.addTag(id, tag)` -> item. Adds a tag (no duplicates). Throws if the item is not found or the tag is empty.
- `list.removeTag(id, tag)` -> item. Removes a tag if present. Throws if the item is not found.
- `list.byTag(tag)` -> item[]. Items carrying the tag.

```js
const a = list.add("Ship release");
list.addTag(a.id, "Work");   // stored as "work"
list.byTag("work");          // [a]
list.removeTag(a.id, "work");
```

### `list.search(query)` -> item[]

Case-insensitive search. The query is split on whitespace and every term must appear in the title or in one of the tags. An empty query returns `[]`.

```js
list.add("Buy milk");
list.addTag(1, "errands");
list.search("MILK");         // matches by title
list.search("buy errands");  // matches by title and tag together
```

### Recurring items

- `list.addRecurring(title, repeat, { due = new Date(), priority } = {})` -> item. Adds an item that repeats `"daily"`, `"weekly"` or `"monthly"`. `due` defaults to now. Throws on an invalid recurrence.
- `list.completeAndReschedule(id)` -> `{ item, next }`. Completes the item; if it recurs (and was not already done), creates the next occurrence with the same title, priority and recurrence and returns it as `next`. Otherwise `next` is `null`.
- `nextDue(due, repeat, day)` -> ISO string. Next due date after `due`. Daily adds 1 day, weekly adds 7 days (UTC). Monthly moves to the next month, clamped to the month's last day; `day` is the anchor day-of-month so Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 31.

```js
const r = list.addRecurring("Water plants", "weekly", { due: "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" });
const { item, next } = list.completeAndReschedule(r.id);
next.due; // "2026-10-08T00:00:00.000Z"
```

### Save / load

- `list.save(path)` writes `{ nextId, items }` as pretty-printed JSON.
- `TodoList.load(path)` (static) reads a file and returns a `TodoList`. Missing fields on items default to `done: false`, `due: null`, `priority: "normal"`, and `nextId` is kept above every existing id. Throws if the file is missing or invalid JSON.

```js
list.save("todo.json");
const again = TodoList.load("todo.json");
```

## CLI

```
node bin/todo.js <command> [args]
```

(or `todo <command>` if linked/installed on your PATH). The list is stored in the file named by the `TODO_FILE` environment variable, defaulting to `./todo.json`. It is created on the first command that saves.

```sh
TODO_FILE=~/work.json node bin/todo.js list
```

Errors are printed to stderr with exit code 1.

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add <title> [--due DATE] [--priority low\|normal\|high]` | Add an item. Multiple title words are joined with spaces. |
| `done <id>` | Complete an item. For recurring items, also creates the next occurrence. |
| `list [--tag TAG]` | Show items in sorted order (see `sorted()`), optionally only those with a tag. |
| `search <query>` | Case-insensitive search of titles and tags; all terms must match. |
| `tag <id> <tag>` | Add a tag to an item. |
| `untag <id> <tag>` | Remove a tag from an item. |
| `recur <id> <daily\|weekly\|monthly\|none>` | Make an item recur, or stop it recurring with `none`. The item needs a due date. |
| `export --json` | Print all items as JSON. |
| `export --csv` | Print all items as CSV with columns `id,title,done,due,priority,tags,repeat` (multiple tags joined by `;`). |

### Examples

```sh
$ todo add Buy milk
added 1: Buy milk

$ todo add File taxes --due 2026-04-15 --priority high
added 2: File taxes

$ todo tag 1 errands
tagged 1: errands

$ todo list
2 [ ] high File taxes (due 2026-04-15)
1 [ ] normal Buy milk #errands

$ todo list --tag errands
1 [ ] normal Buy milk #errands

$ todo search milk errands
1 [ ] normal Buy milk #errands

$ todo untag 1 errands
untagged 1: errands

$ todo recur 2 monthly
recurrence for 2: monthly

$ todo done 2
completed 2: File taxes
next 3: due 2026-05-15

$ todo recur 2 none
recurrence for 2: none

$ todo export --json
$ todo export --csv > todos.csv
```

List output format: `<id> [x| ] <priority> <title> (due YYYY-MM-DD) (<repeat>) #tag #tag`, where the due, repeat and tag parts appear only when set.

I rewrote `README.md` to document the library API and every CLI subcommand, written from `src/todo.js` and `bin/todo.js`. It is the only file I edited, and I didn't run any of the examples.

**Library section**
- It covers the item shape and the exports `PRIORITIES`, `RECURRENCES`, `TodoList` and `nextDue`.
- Every `TodoList` method has a signature, a description and an example where useful: `add`, `complete`, `pending`, `clear`, `sorted`, `addTag`, `removeTag`, `byTag`, `search`, `addRecurring`, `completeAndReschedule`, `save` and static `load`.
- Tags, search, recurring items, due dates, priorities and save/load each have examples.

**CLI section**
- `TODO_FILE` is documented, with a default of `./todo.json`.
- There is a commands table covering `add`, `done`, `list [--tag]`, `search`, `tag`, `untag`, `recur` (including `none`), `export --json` and `export --csv`. The CSV columns are listed.
- A sample session and the `list` output format are included.
- The `recur` entry says an item needs a due date to recur, and the errors-go-to-stderr note says the exit code is 1.

The descriptions state intended behavior, so they should still hold if you fix the code shortly. The sample output in the CLI examples is what I expect the commands to print, not something I ran.
